answer: Sybil resistance comes from bonded identity: each agent locks one indivisible stake, and any identity caught double-voting forfeits the whole bond. The minimum bond is one yarrow token, so it cannot be split; across the ocean of agents every extra vote costs a full stake. An attacker who wants k votes must post k bonds, while an honest agent posts one. Splitting into a glacier of fake names raises cost linearly instead of cheaply, and slashing linked stakes makes the loss total.
